website.note: No dedicated AMoRE website was found; the Center for Underground Physics page describes the experiment (about 2018; it lists the spokespersons Yeongduk Kim and Hongjoo Kim).

name: AMoRE Collaboration
notes: Host: Y2L for AMoRE-Pilot and AMoRE-I, Yemilab for AMoRE-II. No roster was found; the Atlas records no memberships.

summary.plain: The international team (Korea, Russia, Ukraine, China, Germany and others) behind AMoRE, which searches for a hypothetical radioactive decay of molybdenum-100 using crystals cooled to a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero.
summary.technical: AMoRE (Advanced Mo-based Rare process Experiment) Collaboration, led from the IBS Center for Underground Physics: officially formed in 2009 with nine institutions from five countries; the 2015 design report counts about 90 researchers from 17 institutions in eight countries, a CUP page about 90 collaborators from 16 institutions in seven countries. It runs AMoRE-Pilot and AMoRE-I (Y2L) and builds AMoRE-II (Yemilab).
